column1: # Probe-based monotonicity guarantee — simulation over the armed label data.
# Generated by scripts/rd_gap/sim_probe_monotone.py over benchmarks/mono_fit_labels_2026-07-06.tsv
# (24 armed origins, s4-s9 @ q80). date=2026-07-06 host=lilith.
# THE RESULT: a 2-anchor probe {s4,s9} GUARANTEES RD-vs-time monotonicity — it fixes ALL 24
# requested-tier inversions (0 new), INCLUDING pattern-2 (s4 dominates s6/7/8), which the
# feature-gate could NOT separate. The overriding picks are STRICTLY GOOD for the user:
# +0.401 ssim2 better AND the winning encode 1120 ms FASTER than the requested tier. Cost:
# 2.16x total encode wall (encode requested + 2 anchors, keep the best). This is the robust
# complete solution vs the feature-gate's partial (s5-valley only) coverage — it measures
# domination directly instead of predicting it, so pattern-2's non-separability is moot.
# Why the pick is faster: on large content the s6+ bundle makes s6/7/8 SLOWER than s4, so
# the dominator (s4 for pattern-2, s9 for the s5-valley) is both better AND cheaper — the
# probe just has to look. probe-s4 alone fixes 15/24 (misses s5-valley); probe-full fixes
# all 24 but at 5.78x wall — {s4,s9} is the sweet spot.

# requested speed's time budget. dRD=ssim2 gain of overrides; dTime=pick vs requested
